full_judgment:
31. Defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath did not turn up to support the case of the plaintiffs that Ishaque Ali purchased 1.40 acre of land in his name. Plaintiffs however, tried to rely upon an application filed on behalf of Ramendra Nath in the suit. But nobody came forward to prove such application was indeed, filed by defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath. In the absence of any proof, such application could not be treated to be any step taken in the suit by any party in the suit and far less than to be treated as an evidence and was, in fact, not admitted into evidence. 

 51. Had genuineness of any of the copies struck the eyes in any way, then who prevented them to verify the copies with the originals which were not far away from them. Moreover, there was no evidence adduced to create any doubt. Rather, it was the case of the plaintiffs that they came to know that the defendant No. 1's father obtained a decree in respect of the suit land. As Corts of fact, lower Courts are required to give decision on proof, not doubt. Any decision based on doubt cannot be binding and/or sustained in revision. 

 54. It may again be remembered that in a suit for declaration of title only production of deeds of purchase without proof of title and possession of their previous owners within twelve years of the suit would not entitle the plaintiff(s) to any decree. The suit would be doomed to fail. 

 55. But the trial Court appears to have been swayed away when the defendant No. 1 could not say definitely on the 'Pattan' obtained by his father. It reasoned that defendant No. 1 then failed to prove his title. Possession follows title. It forgot to place the burden of proof on right side. 

 56. The defendant No. 1 did not seek any declaration of title in the suit land. It is the plaintiffs who instituted the suit for declaration of their title in the suit land. Burden was therefore, on them to prove their title. Defendant No. 1 just took the defence that he had title in the suit land on the basis of the decree obtained by his father.
